title: San Diego Community Power Rebates 2026: Batteries, Thermostats, EV Charging
desc: What San Diego Community Power pays in 2026: battery $250 to $500 per kWh, thermostat and water heater $50 each, EV Flex Connect, plus free upgrades. SDG&E coupons have ended.
lead: San Diego Community Power's best offer is its battery rebate, which pays $250 to $500 per kWh, more than the SGIP figure an older post of ours used. SDG&E's retail coupons have ended. Several SDCP programs are pilots.
cards_intro: We read San Diego Community Power's pages on October 2, 2026. Several programs are pilots with limited funds. Each card names the fact with the date and a source link.

cards.title: Solar and battery savings
cards.note: $350 market rate or $500 for CARE, FERA or community of concern customers with new solar and battery. $250 or $350 for a new battery added to existing solar. Plus $0.10 per kWh for evening discharge.

cards.title: Smart Energy Rewards
cards.note: $50 upfront for each approved smart thermostat (up to three) and each approved heat pump water heater (up to three), plus a small yearly reward. A pilot.

cards.title: EV Flex Connect
cards.note: Per eligible vehicle, mostly Tesla in the pilot phase, charged at home at least half the time.

cards.title: Equitable Building Decarbonization
cards.note: No-cost upgrades that can include weatherization, a heat pump water heater, heat pump heating and cooling, an electric dryer and an induction cooktop, for income-qualified households in identified communities.

cards.title: SDG&E retail coupons
cards.note: Coupons of $75, $40, $500 and $15 are listed on SDG&E's page, which also says the retail offerings have ended.

sections: San Diego Community Power buys electricity for San Diego, Chula Vista and several other cities, while SDG&E still delivers it. Escondido buys from SDG&E, so SDCP's battery rebate does not apply there. Check your bill for the supplier name.

The battery must be charged by the home's own solar, and the home must be a single-family house. You cannot be enrolled in ELRP or DSGS at the same time. The contractor applies on your behalf. The evening discharge payment of $0.10 per kWh applies when the battery discharges at least half its capacity in the program window. Pilot participants have different rules, so ask for the current terms.

Smart Energy Rewards and EV Flex Connect are pilots. A pilot can close early or change its terms. Enroll early if you want it, and do not buy a device only because of a pilot reward. The $50 thermostat reward is a small bonus, not a reason to switch.

We found no SDCP rebate for a heat pump or insulation, and no general SDG&E heat pump rebate. The Equitable Building Decarbonization program is the main route to a free heat pump, and it is for income-qualified households. State and federal money adds little in 2026. TECH Clean California lists its single-family funds as reserved, the federal home electrification rebates are on hold, and the federal 25C and 25D credits ended after December 31, 2025.
claim_heading: How to claim an SDCP rebate
claim_steps: Confirm your bill shows San Diego Community Power as the supplier.
For a battery, pick a contractor who files the SDCP application for you.
Install the battery so it charges only from the home's solar.
Enroll thermostats and water heaters in Smart Energy Rewards.
If your income qualifies, apply to the Equitable Building Decarbonization program first.

guides: Why the SDG&E rebate is lower
Heat pump or solar first in San Diego?
faq: How much does SDCP pay for a battery?
$250 to $500 per kWh depending on system type and customer type, plus $0.10 per kWh for evening discharge.
Can I use the battery rebate in Escondido?
No. Escondido buys from SDG&E, not SDCP.
Is there a heat pump rebate in San Diego?
We found no open utility rebate. Income-qualified households can get no-cost upgrades through the Equitable Building Decarbonization program.
SDG&E's page says the Golden State Rebates retail offerings have ended.
Do I need solar for the battery rebate?
Yes. The battery must be charged by the home's own solar.
